notes: kb/Work PB5125. §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR14 makes three cases invalid key: (a) random/dynamic key naming an existing record (22), (b) 'When an attempt is made to write beyond the externally defined boundaries of the file' and (c) more significant digits than the relative key (24, §1985:VIII.1.3.4). RelativeConnector#Write implements (a) and (c) at 85 (probes: duplicate random and dynamic keys 22 with the record area kept; sequential and EXTEND release past a PIC 9 key 24 with INVALID KEY run), and (b) for the host file-size boundary via RecordWriteFailed. But a random/dynamic key above HighestRelativeRecordNumber (2,147,483,647, the implementor's highest permitted number) returns FileStatusCode.PermanentBoundary '34' with no edition arm: 1985 has no relative status 34, the write is beyond the file's boundaries, so it must be 24 with the INVALID KEY phrase run. The '34' also sticks as a permanent error, failing the next valid WRITE. kb/Work PB5125 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-39.json).

next.reason: 1985 GR14: invalid key when (a) under random or dynamic access the key names an existing record, (b) 'When an attempt is made to write beyond the externally defined boundaries of the file', (c) the record number has more digits than the relative key. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR33 restates a-c with statuses '22', '24', '24' ('When an attempt is made to write outside the externally defined boundaries of the file'); dropping 'random or dynamic' from (a) changes nothing, since sequential WRITE assigns new numbers. But §2023:14.9.51.4 GR29 takes a random or dynamic WRITE whose relative key 'contains a value that is less than 1 or greater than the highest relative record number permitted for the file' out of the invalid key condition: the WRITE is unsuccessful with status '34', a permanent error. 1985 has no such case and no relative status 34; such a WRITE was an attempt to write beyond the file's boundaries, an invalid key (status 24) that runs the INVALID KEY phrase. Under 2023 the INVALID KEY phrase is not run and the fatal-status rules apply. Different result.
